status: preferred New Moon v2 actor-visible acceptance contract; no native games or competitive qualification

mayUse: own hand, board, discard, attached cards, used-GX/VSTAR state
public opponent board, discard, attached cards, revealed cards and known exact source list
K1 own Prize inference after a legitimate own-deck search
turn, starting orientation, Prize counts, current legal-action surface
mustNotUse: opponent hidden hand identities unless revealed by a legal effect
simulator-only hidden zones unavailable to a paper player

lexicographicDecisionLayers: take an immediate legal game win; avoid an immediate forced loss when a survival action exists
reject mechanically illegal or currently inaccessible actions/lines
preserve or exploit a disappearing action window (Item/Ability/hand-play/evolution window)
score the opponent's strongest immediate reply, including promotion caused by a KO
preserve the selected continuation's required cards/Bench/Energy before paying discard/search costs
compare discrete tactical value and Prize map before raw damage or graph connectivity
only then optimize ordinary setup, draw and damage

cases.state: A legal action takes the final Prize now.
cases.must: Prefer the immediate game-winning action over future lock/setup value.
cases.forbids: Passing a forced win to preserve resources.

cases.state: TPE trigger is resolving; Dragapult ex is a known accessible Apex Dragon payload; candidate target choices include 60-HP Unown/Duskull and nonessential extra Basics.
cases.must: Allow 0, 1, or 2 TPE targets; do not add a second 60-HP Basic without a concrete immediate purpose.
cases.forbids: Always maximizing an 'up to 2' search.

cases.state: Same spread threat, but Duskull is required for a near-term Dusclops response and the evolution/energy continuation is actor-visible.
cases.must: Permit fetching Duskull when the non-Basic continuation outweighs its spread liability.
cases.forbids: A hard-coded never-fetch-60HP rule.

cases.state: Active Regidrago is protected by a copied Covert Flight effect; candidate has a nominal high-damage Basic attack plus one or more legal non-Basic/effect/switch alternatives.
cases.must: Recognize that Basic attack damage is prevented and compare Horror House effect, Dusclops, Escape Rope/Counter Catcher, or another legal target.
cases.forbids: Selecting the Basic damage attack solely by printed damage.

cases.state: AOR and BUS Vileplume are Benched; low-HP Bunnelby is Active; GX unused; a Bunnelby KO and Horror House are both legal.
cases.must: Score BUS Vileplume's immediate promotion after the KO; compare Horror House hand lock before taking the one-Prize KO.
cases.forbids: Treating the KO as pure positive value without the promotion consequence.

cases.state: BUS Vileplume is or will be Active and already has Stealthy Hood attached.
cases.must: Do not credit Cursed Blast as an effective Ability effect on the Hooded BUS target; evaluate non-Ability/non-Basic alternatives.
cases.forbids: Assuming Horror House can retroactively prevent an already attached Hood.

cases.state: The Bunnelby KO takes the candidate's final Prize.
cases.must: Take the win.
cases.forbids: Overriding a final-Prize KO with the promotion-trap heuristic.

cases.state: Candidate goes second; fresh native Gengar & Mimikyu-GX is Active with one Psychic; GX unused; Active Thorns is powered enough to threaten at most one 140-damage hit before candidate's next turn.
cases.must: Recognize Horror House -> survive one hit -> second Psychic -> Poltergeist as a coherent non-Perfection line, subject to actual legality/public state.
cases.forbids: Declaring the matchup locked merely because Perfection is suppressed.

cases.state: Candidate goes first and Gengar has already taken 140 before the candidate's Horror House turn; opponent can attack again from board without hand play.
cases.must: Price the second 140 as lethal before valuing a future Poltergeist turn.
cases.forbids: Assuming Horror House skips the opponent's attack.

cases.state: Klefki is Active, fresh native Gengar is Benched/powered for the next attack, and opponent threatens a 140 attack but no actor-visible gust bypass is currently established.
cases.must: Value the one-Prize buffer and fresh post-KO Gengar promotion as a possible survival line.
cases.forbids: Treating the buffer as unconditional if a legal gust counter is public/available.

cases.state: Two opposing Garbodor are each Tool-enabled and suppressing Abilities; one Field Blower is playable; a Stadium is also a desirable target.
cases.must: If choosing the Perfection-restoration line, target both Garbodor Tools before the optional Stadium.
cases.forbids: Removing Stadium + one Tool and then assuming Perfection is restored.

cases.state: All live Garbotoxin Tools can be removed now; Mewtwo/Gengar Horror House is legal after removal; opponent has future hand-based retool capacity.
cases.must: Compare Field Blower -> Horror House against immediate damage, crediting the protected no-retool hand-lock turn.
cases.forbids: Scoring Field Blower only as an instantaneous Tool removal.

cases.state: Three Garbodor are simultaneously Tool-enabled; only one Field Blower is available.
cases.must: Reject a Perfection line that depends on one Blower disabling all three.
cases.forbids: Treating partial Tool removal as full Garbotoxin release.

cases.state: Before game start, candidate has at least two Basics available for Active/Bench setup.
cases.must: Put at least one Basic on the Bench; avoid a voluntary lone-Active loss exposure.
cases.forbids: Keeping every extra Basic in hand for ordinary resource efficiency.

cases.state: Klefki and at least one other Basic are available during setup.
cases.must: Strongly prefer Klefki Active plus a Benched survivor unless a concrete stronger exception exists; recognize Cologne as opponent counter.
cases.forbids: Treating Mischievous Lock as an absolute donk prevention.

cases.state: New Moon receives a normal setup turn before rank26's first attack and would otherwise end with no Bench; TPE or Basic search is legal.
cases.must: Spend sufficient setup resources to create a Bench before passing.
cases.forbids: Saving search/TPE for later while leaving an immediate no-Pokémon loss condition.

cases.state: One or more Shadow Rider VMAX are evolved and operating; candidate can promote Klefki; Mewtwo & Mew-GX Perfection is relevant.
cases.must: Recognize Klefki does not suppress Evolution VMAX Underworld Door and does suppress own Basic Perfection.
cases.forbids: Scoring Klefki as universal Ability lock.

cases.state: Candidate has Solrock + Lunatone OBF in play and can play Path to the Peak.
cases.must: Recognize Path suppresses opponent Rule-Box Abilities while Lunatone's New Moon protects candidate Pokémon from Stadium effects.
cases.forbids: Treating Path as symmetric self-lock in this exact candidate board.

cases.state: Path is active, Horror House hand lock is available/applied, and opponent Marshadow UNB is already on the Bench.
cases.must: Expect Resetting Hole to remain a board Ability that can discard Path; do not credit Horror House with stopping it.
cases.forbids: Conflating hand lock with in-play Ability lock.

cases.state: Candidate has asymmetric Path setup; opponent Marshadow is not publicly in play; Horror House is legal.
cases.must: Credit Horror House with blocking hand-played Marshadow, Field Blower and replacement Stadium during the locked turn, without assuming those hidden cards are actually in hand.
cases.forbids: Using hidden-hand knowledge to claim a specific out was denied.

cases.state: Secret Box is mechanically legal and only three other hand cards exist, but one is the only Energy required for the chosen attack continuation.
cases.must: Reject Secret Box for that intended continuation unless another coherent line justifies changing plans.
cases.forbids: Treating three physical cards as three acceptable discards.

cases.state: Secret Box is legal; at least three actor-visible cards are genuinely dead/redundant for the selected horizon (for example post-turn-one VIP Pass with no remaining role); fetched bundle advances the selected continuation.
cases.must: Permit the Box line and record why each discard is acceptable.
cases.forbids: Permanent card-name 'never discard' rules detached from state.

cases.state: Secret Box can fetch Field Blower but paying the cost would discard the only accessible Gengar donor required for the intended Blower -> Horror House line.
cases.must: Reject that Box route or explicitly select a different continuation.
cases.forbids: Counting Box->Blower access as success after destroying its follow-up.

cases.state: Current attacker/line is already functional; TPE can fetch extra low-impact support Basics such as Unown/Duskull; opponent has Snorlax Block plus repeated gust capacity.
cases.must: Allow zero or one TPE target and preserve a narrow Bench when the extra body is primarily a future trap target.
cases.forbids: Maximizing Bench occupancy for generic setup value.

cases.state: Singleton Escape Rope is available but no current Block trap requires it; opponent retains public/source-known gust capacity.
cases.must: Price Escape Rope as future Block insurance before spending it for minor positioning.
cases.forbids: Treating the singleton switch as ordinary low-value mobility.

cases.state: Unown AOR 30 is Active against 150-HP Snorlax PGO 55 with Block operating.
cases.must: Recognize normal retreat is prohibited and 10-damage Hidden Power is not a quick escape; prioritize a legal switch/board-release plan.
cases.forbids: Assuming Energy attachments eventually permit retreat through Block.

cases.state: Duskull is trapped Active, but Dusclops and the required Energy/evolution timing are actor-visible and achievable.
cases.must: Recognize the developed Stage-1 attack route as a possible board-release line.
cases.forbids: Hardcoding Escape Rope as the only response to every Block trap.

cases.family: Temple of Sinnoh / Special Energy timing
cases.state: Temple of Sinnoh is active; candidate legally attaches Telepathic Psychic Energy from hand to a Psychic Pokémon with available Bench space.
cases.must: Allow the attachment-time TPE search for up to two Basic Psychic Pokémon, while separately tracking Temple's suppression after attachment.
cases.forbids: Treating Temple as canceling the attachment-time search trigger.

cases.family: Temple of Sinnoh / Special Energy timing
cases.state: Temple remains active; candidate has one attached TPE and no other Psychic-providing Energy; a Psychic-cost attack such as Horror House is being considered.
cases.must: Treat the attached TPE as Colorless under Temple and require another legal Psychic source or Stadium removal/replacement before the attack.
cases.forbids: Equating successful TPE setup with a currently paid Psychic attack cost.

cases.state: Silent Lab is active and candidate has Solrock + Lunatone OBF in play; Mewtwo & Mew-GX Perfection is relevant.
cases.must: Treat Lunatone's Basic Ability New Moon as removed by Silent Lab and Perfection as suppressed.
cases.forbids: Generalizing the Path-to-the-Peak asymmetry to Silent Lab.

cases.state: Silent Lab is active; candidate has a legal own-Stadium replacement and an Ability-dependent attack continuation.
cases.must: Price Stadium replacement/removal as a prerequisite to the Ability-dependent line.
cases.forbids: Spending resources on Solrock/Lunatone as if the pair alone clears Silent Lab.

cases.state: Silent Lab and AOR Vileplume Item lock are simultaneously active.
cases.must: Treat Field Blower as inaccessible while Item lock holds and search for a legal non-Item/pre-lock Stadium solution.
cases.forbids: Hallucinating a live Field Blower answer under Item lock.

cases.state: Opposing Klefki is Active; opposing Electrode-GX is Benched and otherwise able to use Extra Energy Bomb; candidate Mewtwo & Mew-GX and Lunatone Abilities are relevant.
cases.must: Recognize Klefki suppresses Basic Perfection and Basic New Moon, but does not suppress Stage-1 Electrode-GX.
cases.forbids: Treating opposing Klefki as symmetrical shutdown of Electrode-GX or treating Lunatone as active under Klefki.

cases.state: Native Gengar & Mimikyu-GX is attack-ready with GX unused; Path to the Peak is playable; opposing Electrode-GX is live; no actor-visible board-only Stadium removal is established.
cases.must: Compare Path -> native Horror House-GX against Cologne/Perfection, crediting Path's suppression of Electrode and Horror House's denial of hand-played Stadium/evolution answers.
cases.forbids: Requiring Perfection or Cologne merely because opposing Klefki suppresses Mewtwo.

cases.state: Rank-17 Marshadow UNB 81 is already on the Bench while Path/Horror House is being considered.
cases.must: Expect Resetting Hole to remain a board Ability that can discard Path despite Horror House.
cases.forbids: Conflating hand lock with in-play Ability lock.

cases.state: A legal TPE/Bench choice would add unnecessary low-HP or multi-Prize bodies while the source can plausibly reach a Telescopic-Sight Electro Rain Bomb turn.
cases.must: Allow 0/1 TPE targets and price each Bench body by Electro Rain packets-to-KO plus Prize yield; prefer discard-zone Gengar donor over an unnecessary Benched donor when legal.
cases.forbids: Maximizing Bench/search connectivity without scoring distributed Prize conversion.

cases.state: No Prize changes yet; both candidate Dusclops can use Cursed Blast and self-KO before the opponent's first Electrode Bomb; their counter placement does not take an opposing Prize.
cases.must: Recognize two self-KOs make the first Bomb restore 4-4 Prize parity, so Reversal/Counter Energy Prize-deficit multipliers are off after that Bomb unless another Prize change occurs.
cases.forbids: Assuming the first Bomb always activates Reversal/Counter multipliers.

cases.state: Exactly one candidate Cursed Blast self-KO occurred before the opponent's first Electrode Bomb and no other Prize changes occurred.
cases.must: Recognize the post-Bomb state is candidate 4 Prizes remaining vs Raichu 5, so Raichu is still behind and Reversal/Counter multipliers remain live.
cases.forbids: Treating one self-KO as sufficient Prize-parity control.

cases.state: Candidate goes second on its first turn; Horror House-GX is legal; opponent has not yet legally evolved Voltorb/Pikachu on its first turn.
cases.must: Value Horror House as denial of the next hand-play evolution/Bomb-combo turn, not merely generic hand disruption.
cases.forbids: Waiting for Electrode/Raichu to exist before valuing the lock.

cases.state: K1 shows both Dusclops are Prized; BUS Vileplume is Active; AOR Vileplume is Benched and Item lock is live; Guzma is legally available; opponent has a legal Bench target.
cases.must: Use or seriously score the Supporter switch that moves BUS off Active so Basic attackers can function; do not declare the board structurally attack-locked solely because both Dusclops are Prized.
cases.forbids: Relying on Item switch/gust through AOR lock or on a Prized Dusclops.

cases.state: Cursed Blast self-KO has put New Moon behind on Prizes; Ace Trainer and Counter Catcher are both legal and useful; Guzma is also available.
cases.must: Preserve the option to play Ace Trainer plus Counter Catcher in the same turn and compare that multi-axis line against Guzma.
cases.forbids: Replacing the Item gust with Guzma merely because both gust, thereby losing the Ace Trainer action.

cases.state: New Moon survived the source's Prize-donation plan and has one Prize remaining while the opponent has fewer remaining Prizes than required for Counter Catcher to be legal; a gusted target can yield the last Prize.
cases.must: Recognize Counter Catcher is disabled by Prize state and evaluate Guzma as the no-Prize-condition gust.
cases.forbids: Assuming Counter Catcher remains active simply because it is in hand.

cases.state: A support Pokémon is trapped Active by Snorlax Block; both Guzma and Escape Rope are legal alternatives; candidate has a Bench.
cases.must: Compare Supporter contention and future singleton-Rope value; recognize Guzma as a functional own-switch because it also switches the opponent's Active.
cases.forbids: Treating Counter Catcher as an own-switch or preserving Guzma solely because it is a Supporter.

cases.state: Silent Lab is active and Guzma is not already in hand; Tapu Lele-GX Wonder Tag would otherwise be the intended Supporter search.
cases.must: Treat Wonder Tag as unavailable while Silent Lab suppresses Basic Abilities; first establish a legal Stadium removal/replacement or use another real access route.
cases.forbids: Hallucinating Tapu Lele-to-Guzma through Silent Lab.

cases.state: A line depends on candidate-owned Stadium availability or replacement count.
cases.must: Use the actual v2 count of three own Stadiums: one Sky Field and two Path to the Peak.
cases.forbids: Inheriting the v1 fixture assumption of two Sky Field / four own Stadiums.

cases.state: AOR Vileplume is in play, Stoutland BCR is Active, candidate Items and Supporters are locked, Lillie's Clefairy ex has two Energy, and total Benched Pokémon across both sides is at least 6.
cases.must: Recognize Full Moon Rondo reaches at least 140 and cleanly KOs Stoutland, reopening Supporters after the lock Pokémon leaves Active.
cases.forbids: Treating simultaneous Item+Supporter lock as preventing attacks or requiring an Item/Supporter unlock first.

cases.state: Same dual-lock board, clean 140-HP Stoutland, Clefairy has two Energy, total Benched Pokémon across both sides is at most 5.
cases.must: Calculate Full Moon Rondo below 140 and compare prior damage/another attacker.
cases.forbids: Hallucinating the six-Bench breakpoint.

cases.state: AOR Vileplume's Irritating Pollen is active; Powerglass is in hand and has a legal Tool target; no separate Tool lock is active.
cases.must: Keep Powerglass legally playable because Pokémon Tools are not Items under the current rules.
cases.forbids: Applying Item lock to Pokémon Tool cards.

cases.state: Rank2 Bunnelby is Active, AOR Vileplume is live, Stoutland is Benched, and candidate can take the Bunnelby KO.
cases.must: Score Stoutland's immediate promotion and resulting Sentinel lock, then permit the KO if the selected continuation can remove Stoutland without Item/Supporter help.
cases.forbids: Treating the one-Prize KO as pure upside or using a universal never-KO rule.

cases.state: Candidate goes second on its first turn; Horror House-GX is legal; Grand Tree is already in play from rank2's first turn.
cases.must: Compare replacing Grand Tree before Horror House, since Horror House blocks hand plays but does not disable an already-in-play Stadium effect.
cases.forbids: Assuming hand lock switches off Grand Tree.

cases.state: Bunnelby is Active under Horror House with sufficient attached Energy to retreat; Stoutland is Benched.
cases.must: Expect ordinary retreat as a board action and Stoutland promotion even though cards cannot be played from hand.
cases.forbids: Treating Horror House as an Active-position lock.

cases.state: Dual lock is active; candidate can use direct Clefairy/Latias attacks; opponent Pidgeot ex or Vileplume-GX Ability is live; Path is playable.
cases.must: Recognize Path can suppress Rule-Box support even though it does not suppress AOR Vileplume/Stoutland; compare its low self-cost when the selected attack needs no candidate Rule-Box Ability.
cases.forbids: Scoring Path only by whether it removes the two lock Abilities.

cases.state: Candidate goes first and has its pre-lock turn before rank2 can execute its going-second TM Evolution setup; attacker/Powerglass/Basic-Psychic-discard setup competes with generic board expansion.
cases.must: Prefer preserving a credible in-lock attacker economy when it dominates low-impact setup.
cases.forbids: Burning the disappearing Item/setup window on generic access that becomes unusable under Vileplume.

cases.state: AOR Vileplume is already live, Bunnelby is still Active after the TM Evolution turn, Stoutland is Benched, Guzma is legal because Sentinel is not yet Active, and candidate has a credible attack on Stoutland.
cases.must: Compare Guzma as a disappearing pre-Sentinel Supporter window: gust Stoutland before it becomes Active and, if the attack line is funded, remove it before Supporter lock begins.
cases.forbids: Saving Guzma for a future turn after Stoutland is Active and Sentinel has made Supporters unplayable.

cases.state: Opponent Sudowoodo GRI 66 Roadblock is active and candidate TPE resolves with fewer than two legal Bench slots under the four-Bench cap.
cases.must: Respect the live Bench cap and choose at most the number of open slots; allow fewer or zero targets.
cases.forbids: Resolving TPE as if the ordinary five-Bench limit still applied.

cases.state: Candidate Active Klefki currently suppresses opposing Basic Sudowoodo Roadblock; candidate has expanded above four Benched Pokémon while Roadblock is off; a retreat/Guzma/other move would take Klefki out of Active.
cases.must: Price Roadblock reactivation as part of the switch: once the opposing Ability returns, candidate must reduce to four Benched Pokémon under the printed continuous effect.
cases.forbids: Using temporary Klefki suppression to build a five-plus Bench and then switching Klefki away without accounting for forced Bench reduction.

cases.state: Opposing Sudowoodo Roadblock is active and Path to the Peak is available.
cases.must: Recognize Path does not suppress the non-Rule-Box Sudowoodo Ability; use Path only for other Rule-Box targets.
cases.forbids: Treating Path as a universal Ability-lock answer.

cases.state: Opposing Empoleon V is Active; candidate Solrock + Lunatone OBF are in play; Mewtwo & Mew-GX Perfection is relevant; Path to the Peak is playable.
cases.must: Before Path, Emperor's Eyes suppresses non-Rule-Box Basic Lunatone but spares Rule-Box Mewtwo. After Path suppresses Empoleon V's Rule-Box Ability, re-evaluate continuous effects: Lunatone can regain New Moon and, with Solrock, protect candidate Pokémon from Path.
cases.forbids: Freezing the pre-Path Ability state or assuming Emperor's Eyes suppresses Rule-Box Mewtwo.

cases.state: Candidate is under Chimecho CIN 43 Bell of Silence for the turn; Guzma is not already in hand; the intended access route was playing Tapu Lele-GX from hand for Wonder Tag.
cases.must: Reject the Tapu-Lele-from-hand route because Bell of Silence forbids playing Pokémon with Abilities from hand; compare direct draw, Secret Box/FSS if legal, or a line that does not require that hand-played Ability Pokémon.
cases.forbids: Treating Wonder Tag as available simply because Tapu Lele is searchable.

cases.state: Opposing Dusknoir PRE 37 can use Cursed Blast for 13 damage counters and self-KO; candidate is choosing whether to Bench a 60-HP support Basic for generic future value.
cases.must: Price the support Basic as an immediate damage-counter KO target and update the Prize map for both the Dusknoir self-KO and any candidate KO; prefer a narrower Bench when the extra body has no concrete near-term role.
cases.forbids: Treating Stage-2 damage-counter Ability pressure as ordinary attack spread or as free opponent self-KO value.

requiredBeforeNativeInvestment: pure or synthetic actor-visible tests covering all cases in this v2 contract
trace exposes selected continuation, strongest competing action, protected resources, Stadium count and any Secret Box discard reasons
TPE target resolver can legally return 0, 1 or 2 targets
policy explicitly conditions on opponent Ability source stage/type and public board position
no case relies on opponent hidden-hand or face-down-Prize identities except own K1 Prize inference
no native/full-game dispatch until the repository's current owner/CI gates permit it
